name: PyPI
description: Python Package Index: project and release metadata, dependencies and Python compatibility, distribution files with hashes, PEP 740 provenance, release feeds, the global change log, a user's projects and site statistics.

tools.name: Changelog
tools.description: Incrementally track everything that changes on PyPI: poll with the last seen serial. Upstream serves up to 50 000 events per call; `limit` windows them and `next_serial` resumes.

options.name: since_serial
options.about: Return events with a serial greater than this (use `next_serial` or `head_serial` from a previous call).

response.about: PyPI's global change log over XML-RPC (`changelog_since_serial`): every event (new release, file added, project created, yanked, removed, ...) after a serial, with project, version, timestamp, action and serial, plus the current head serial. Without `since_serial` it returns only the head so a caller can start polling.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.about: Unix seconds (UTC).

fields.name: version
fields.about: Null for project-level events.

tools.name: Files
tools.description: Enumerate all files across all versions of a package (for mirroring, hash pinning or compatibility scans), or get the complete version list cheaply.

options.name: cursor
options.about: `next_cursor` from the previous page; omit for the first page.

options.name: project
options.about: Project name as on PyPI, any spelling: PEP 503 normalization (case-insensitive, `-`/`_`/`.` equivalent) is applied before the request. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$.

response.about: Every distribution file of a project from the Simple repository API (PEP 691 JSON, `/simple/{project}/`): filename, download URL, sha256, size, upload time, `requires_python`, yanked state and provenance URL, plus the full version list and project status. The index has no server pages; `cursor`/`limit` window the file list.

fields.name: provenance_url
fields.about: Integrity API URL when the file has attestations; null otherwise.

tools.name: Project
tools.description: Look up a Python package by name or pasted pypi.org URL: what it is, who publishes it, which Python versions and dependencies it needs, which versions exist, and whether the current release has advisories.

options.name: include_description
options.about: Also return the long description (README, often tens of KB).

options.name: project
options.about: Project name as on PyPI, any spelling: PEP 503 normalization (case-insensitive, `-`/`_`/`.` equivalent) is applied before the request. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$.

options.name: url
options.about: A pasted https://pypi.org/project/{name}/ (or /pypi/{name}/json) URL; alternative to `project`.

response.about: One project from the JSON API (`/pypi/{project}/json`): identity, latest-release metadata (summary, license, author, `requires_python`, `requires_dist` dependencies with extras markers, classifiers, project URLs), every release version with file count, first upload time and yanked state, the latest release's files with sizes and hashes, and known vulnerabilities for the latest release.

fields.name: classifiers
fields.about: Trove classifiers.

fields.name: description
fields.about: Long description (README) only when `include_description` is true; otherwise omitted.

fields.name: files
fields.about: Files of the latest release.

fields.name: last_serial
fields.about: PyPI's global change serial at which this project last changed (also `x-pypi-last-serial`).

fields.name: license
fields.about: Free-text `License` metadata field; null when the project uses `license_expression` or declares none.

fields.name: license_expression
fields.about: SPDX expression (`License-Expression`, PEP 639); null for older metadata.

fields.name: license_files
fields.about: `License-File` entries; null when not declared.

fields.name: name
fields.about: Project name as PyPI stores it (canonical spelling).

fields.name: normalized_name
fields.about: PEP 503 normalized name used in URLs.

fields.name: project_url
fields.about: https://pypi.org/project/{normalized_name}/

fields.name: project_urls
fields.about: `Project-URL` entries (Documentation, Source, ...); null when none are declared.

fields.name: provides_extra
fields.about: Optional dependency groups; null when none are declared.

fields.name: release_url
fields.about: https://pypi.org/project/{normalized_name}/{version}/

fields.name: requires_dist
fields.about: Dependencies as PEP 508 requirement strings (extras carry `; extra == "name"` markers). Null when the metadata declares none.

fields.name: requires_python
fields.about: `Requires-Python` specifier, e.g. `>=3.8`; null when not declared.

fields.name: version
fields.about: Release version this metadata describes (the latest non-yanked release for `project`).

fields.name: version_count
fields.about: Number of release versions PyPI lists.

fields.name: versions
fields.about: Every release version in PyPI's listing order (string-sorted, not PEP 440-sorted).

fields.name: vulnerabilities
fields.about: Advisories affecting the latest release (from OSV via PyPI).

vulnerabilities.details:
### Impact

Due to a URL parsing issue, Requests releases prior to 2.32.4 may leak .netrc credentials to third parties for specific maliciously-crafted URLs.

### Workarounds
For older versions of Requests, use of the .netrc file can be disabled with `trust_env=False` on your Requests Session ([docs](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.Session.trust_env)).

### References
https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6965
https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2025/Jun/2

### Impact
The `requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths()` utility function uses a predictable filename when extracting files from zip archives into the system temporary directory. If the target file already exists, it is reused without validation. A local attacker with write access to the temp directory could pre-create a malicious file that would be loaded in place of the legitimate one.

### Affected usages
**Standard usage of the Requests library is not affected by this vulnerability.** Only applications that call `extract_zipped_paths()` directly are impacted.

### Remediation
Upgrade to at least Requests 2.33.0, where the library now extracts files to a non-deterministic location.

If developers are unable to upgrade, they can set `TMPDIR` in their environment to a directory with restricted write access.

Due to a URL parsing issue, Requests releases prior to 2.32.4 may leak .netrc credentials to third parties for specific maliciously-crafted URLs.

### Workarounds
For older versions of Requests, use of the .netrc file can be disabled with `trust_env=False` on your Requests Session ([docs](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.Session.trust_env)).

https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6965
https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2025/Jun/2

Requests is a HTTP library. Prior to version 2.33.0, the `requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths()` utility function uses a predictable filename when extracting files from zip archives into the system temporary directory. If the target file already exists, it is reused without validation. A local attacker with write access to the temp directory could pre-create a malicious file that would be loaded in place of the legitimate one. Standard usage of the Requests library is not affected by this vulnerability. Only applications that call `extract_zipped_paths()` directly are impacted. Starting in version 2.33.0, the library extracts files to a non-deterministic location. If developers are unable to upgrade, they can set `TMPDIR` in their environment to a directory with restricted write access.

tools.name: Stats
tools.description: Size PyPI as a whole or see which projects dominate its storage.

response.about: PyPI-wide storage statistics (`/stats/` JSON): total size of all packages and the 100 largest projects by total file size.

fields.name: size
fields.about: Bytes.

tools.name: User projects
tools.description: Find every package published or maintained by a given PyPI username (from a project's ownership or maintainer links).

response.about: Projects a PyPI user owns or maintains, over XML-RPC `user_packages`: name and role (Owner or Maintainer). The HTML profile page is behind Fastly's Client Challenge, and PyPI returns an empty list for an unknown username, so an empty result carries a warning rather than `not_found`.
